text:
maria (Docs): Hi team — opened a PR with the Dedicated Capacity migration guide + a Terraform example for provisioning reserved pools. Need a quick pass on the SLA matrix row and the wording around data isolation. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/1294

sam (Eng): thanks — will skim. Which SLA row specifically?

maria (Docs): the "burst fallback" row — I adjusted latency targets for burst capacity but not sure about the wording for billing impact.

jon (Platform): I can confirm the latency targets, but billing note needs to say "pro-rated for burst minutes beyond committed throughput" not "per-request".

anya (SRE): also please add a note about isolation: ephemeral KV caches are per-tenant on Dedicated, but shared infra metrics are aggregated. We should be explicit.

maria (Docs): good call. Proposed sentence: "Dedicated pools provide tenant-isolated model execution and cache state; operational telemetry is aggregated for platform health while maintaining tenant-level access controls." ok to add?

sam (Eng): yep that's accurate. Maybe add a short bullet about network isolation (VPC peering) and KMS scope.

maria (Docs): added both bullets — can someone sanity-check the Terraform snippet?

alex (Support): leaving for sam/jon to verify infra bits, but I noticed a broken internal link to the Dedicated pricing page in the migration checklist. PR has it currently as: https://internal.redwood/pricing/dedicated (404)

maria (Docs): thanks — updated link to the new pricing doc: https://internal.redwood/pricing/dedicated-reserved. Good catch.

sam (Eng): Terraform snippet looks fine, small nit: resource name should be "redwood_dedicated_pool" (not "dedicated_pool"). Here's a minimal example to paste in: 

```terraform
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "app-prod" {
  name             = "app-prod"
  gpu_type         = "a100-80gb"
  min_capacity     = 2
  max_capacity     = 10
  burst_policy     = "enabled"
  kms_key_id       = "arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd"
}
```

maria (Docs): perfect — I swapped that in. Also added a short SDK snippet for Python provisioning via our infra client. jon, can you confirm the example uses the right client method?

jon (Platform): looks good. For the SDK the call is create_pool(...) and accept a provisioning_options dict — sample is fine but change param name to "provisioning_config" in the snippet.

maria (Docs): updated. Pasting final SDK example included in the PR: 

```python
from redwood import InfraClient
client = InfraClient()
conf = {"gpu_type": "a100-80gb", "min_capacity": 2, "max_capacity": 10, "burst_policy": "enabled"}
pool = client.create_pool(name="app-prod", provisioning_config=conf)
print(pool.id)
```

anya (SRE): one more ops note: emphasize that canary deploys to Dedicated use a traffic-split route and will respect the pool's isolation settings — added a short paragraph under rollouts.

maria (Docs): awesome — added. Anything else before I merge?

sam (Eng): quick grammar nit in the SLA table: change "uptime target: 99.9% (excl. scheduled maint)" to "Uptime SLA: 99.9% (excl. scheduled maintenance)".

maria (Docs): fixed.

alex (Support): approving copy for customer-facing bits. 

jon (Platform): approved for infra accuracy.

deploy-bot: build status — docs CI passed (link: https://ci.internal/builds/4821) :white_check_mark:

maria (Docs): thanks everyone — merging after CI. Will follow up with a short migration checklist email to customers and post the link in #customer-success. :tada:
